Alex K.: Quick check-in — noticed a 12-18% host-side CPU bump on the canary for preparse + streaming. Dumped a short pprof; wondering if this is kernel selection noise or pure parse/IO overhead. cc @Priya @Jordan

Priya S.: I pulled the pprof. Top lines: ```
38% parse::Tokenize
22% grpc::Writev
15% kvcache::SerializeKey
10% kernel::choose_kernels
5% http2::small_write_hpack
```
Looks like tokenization + writev are the big wins.

Jordan L.: grpc::Writev + small_write_hpack screams many tiny frames. Streaming chunker seems to be flushing per-token in the canary. Are we sending per-token small writes (<=512 bytes)?

Devon M.: We changed chunking to immediate-flush for low-latency mode last month (flag: `stream.chunker.flush_immediate=true`). That reduces tail latency but increases syscall/writev overhead. Maybe the canary hit a workload with many short messages.

Alex K.: Can we try: 1) toggle `flush_immediate=false` on canary 2) enable socket coalesce (linger=1ms) 3) run kernel hint disabled (force kernel selection to default) — to separate parse vs kernel costs?

Priya S.: Agree. I also saw kvcache::SerializeKey spikes correlated with parse time. Possible repeated key regen on short requests (prefix length variance). I'll add instrumentation to expose kvcache misses per-request.

Jordan L.: Small experiment suggestion: change chunker to accumulate up to 2KB or 8 tokens before flush. Quick patch: ```diff
- if (chunk.size() > 0) flush();
+ if (chunk.byte_size() >= 2048 || chunk.token_count() >= 8) flush();
```
This should reduce writev calls by ~3x for the observed sample.

Devon M.: Also check kernel::choose_kernels path — it's at 10% which is surprising. Might be heavy heuristics when sequence length distribution is noisy. Could be recomputing fingerprints every request. We can cache kernel decisions keyed by `(model_id, seq_len_bucket)` for 10s.

Priya S.: Will instrument kernel selection cache hit rate. If we get >80% misses, that's the source of the 10%.

Alex K.: Action items: Priya -> add kvcache miss counter and kernel-selection-cache metric. Jordan -> deploy small-chunk-coalesce patch to canary. Devon -> flip `flush_immediate` and try socket coalesce in parallel. I'll run A/B and post results here.

deploy-bot: Canary update: preparse-serializer-slim-bench patch v2 deployed to canary (id: canary-224). Monitoring: CPU up 15% (baseline), writev rate x3.

Jordan L.: Noted cpu/writev increase. If coalesce patch lands, should see writev down and parse fraction go up/down depending.

Priya S.: Quick note on telemetry: when running the trace, include `rpc.writev_count`, `kv.serialize_time_ms`, `parse.tokenize_time_ms`, `kernel.choice_ms`. That makes the triage much faster.

Devon M.: If coalescing shows regression on tail latency for single-token prompts we can make it adaptive: coalesce only when request_rate > 50rps or token_rate > 2000tps.

Alex K.: Sounds good. I'll coordinate the A/B for 1 hour ramp and report. If coalesce reduces writev by >2x and CPU drops >=8% we keep it. Otherwise roll back. :thumbsup:
